proposals.before: In the tenth month of year 4, on dingwei day, Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; with Huan He of Changlu he joined the Mount Tai bandits Zhang He and Yan, rallied at Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as their leader; the court ordered Prince Wei Yuan of Huaiyang and others to suppress them.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of year 4, on dingwei day, Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; with Huan He of Changlu he joined the Mount Tai bandits Zhang Heyan, rallied at Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as their leader; the court ordered Prince Wei Yuan of Huaiyang and others to suppress them.

proposals.before: In the tenth month of the fourth year, on the day dingwei, the commoner Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; together with Huan He of Changlu he linked with the bandit chiefs Zhang He and Yan of Mount Tai and others, gathered a band to hold Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as leader; an edict ordered Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan and others to attack them.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of the fourth year, on the day dingwei, the commoner Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; together with Huan He of Changlu he linked with the bandit chiefs Zhang Heyan of Mount Tai and others, gathered a band to hold Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as leader; an edict ordered Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan and others to attack them.

proposals.before: In the fourth month, Muru Chen, Prince of Yidu and Governor of Yong Province, was guilty and granted death.

proposals.reason: Chinese 癸酋 (for 癸酉) is guiyou, not yiyou (乙酉).

proposals.reason: Chinese 癸酋 (for 癸酉) is guiyou, not yiyou (乙酉).

decisions.reason: 太山羣盜張和顏等 treats 張和顏 as one personal name (surname 張 + given name 和顏) followed by 等; splitting into Zhang He and Yan invents a second person.
The same Chinese name 張和顏 is a single bandit leader; literal Zhang He and Yan is an unwarranted split.
宜都王目辰 is the two-character name 目辰 (Muchen); Muru Chen invents a false multi-syllable surname not present in the Chinese.
Literal likewise misreads 目辰 as Muru Chen; Muchen restores the Chinese name.
万俟醜奴 is the compound Xianbei surname 万俟 plus given name 醜奴; Moyechou Nu garbles the surname and splits the name.
Literal Moyechou Nu similarly mistranslates 万俟醜奴; Wanqi Chounu matches the Chinese name.
出帝太昌元年 names the Departed Emperor of the Taichang era—Emperor Xiaowu—not 孝靜 Emperor Xiaojing, who appears separately later in the chapter.
This 出帝 under Yongxi 3 is again Emperor Xiaowu; Xiaojing is a different ruler and cannot stand here.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 出帝為斛斯椿等諸佞關構

decisions.reason: 出帝為斛斯椿等迫脅…出於長安 is Xiaowu’s flight west; Xiaojing is the later Eastern Wei emperor, not this subject.
肅宗熙平元年 opens the reign attribution; idiomatic English omitted 肅宗 (Emperor Xiaoming), which the literal already renders.
安頡 is An Xie (頡 = xie); An Qi is a wrong reading of 頡.
Literal An Qi likewise misreads 頡; An Xie is the correct romanization.
延昌 romanizes as Yanchang; Yanzhang is a misspelling of the era name.
Literal Yanzhang is the same misspelling of 延昌; Yanchang is required.
延昌二年 again requires Yanchang, not Yanzhang.
Literal likewise misspells 延昌 as Yanzhang; Yanchang is correct.
延昌元年 must be Yanchang 1; Yanzhang is a misspelling.
Literal Yanzhang again misspells 延昌; Yanchang restores the era name.

decisions.after: In the eleventh month, on yiyou day, [5] Moyuan Liang Hehoudou of the Rouran led seven hundred men and women to surrender.
decisions.reason: 莫緣 is the Rouran title and 梁賀侯豆 the personal name, so separating Moyuan from Liang Hehoudou is right; but 男女七百口 is men and women only—the proposed after still invents children.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蠕蠕莫緣梁賀侯豆率男女七百口來降

decisions.reason: Literal correctly separates title 莫緣 from personal name 梁賀侯豆; Moyuan Liang Hehoudou matches the Chinese segmentation.
出帝 here is Emperor Xiaowu; calque Emperor Chu invents a false name Chu and obscures the same referent already corrected in the idiomatic.
Literal Emperor Chu for 出帝 likewise invents a false name; Emperor Xiaowu is the historical referent of this 出帝.
Same 出帝 fleeing to Chang'an is Xiaowu; replacing the Chu calque corrects the literal referent.
六年七月庚寅朔 is the seventh month; idiomatic sixth month contradicts 七月.
Literal sixth month likewise misreads 七月; seventh month is required.
Collation quote 癸酋 stands for 癸酉 (guiyou); yiyou would be 乙酉, a different stem-branch.
Literal yiyou misreads 癸酋/癸酉 as 乙酉; guiyou is the correct day name.
延昌二年 in the collation head must be Yanchang, not Yanzhang.
Literal Yanzhang is the same misspelling of 延昌; Yanchang is correct.
齊獻武王 carries the full posthumous compound 獻武 (Xianwu); Prince Xian of Qi drops 武.
Literal likewise truncates 獻武 to Xian; Prince Xianwu of Qi preserves the full posthumous title.
